headline: Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias made landfall near Destin, FL around Fri, Oct 9, 8 PM CT. Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias: 35 mph, 32.8N 86.8W, inland, moving NNW at 12 mph. The center is over land.

gulf.text: NHC is issuing advisories on this system; see the storm panel.

google.text: 14 of 50 ensemble members forecast a track so far. 14 of 14 bring the center to the Louisiana-to-Florida coast (FL 14), typically around Sat, Oct 10, 1 AM CT. 0 of 14 reach hurricane strength; typical peak 50 mph.

keyMessages: Heavy rainfall associated with post-tropical cyclone Isaias will continue across the Southern Appalachians and Southeast today. Considerable flash and urban flooding will be possible. Landslides are also possible across the Southern Appalachians.

Strong wind gusts continue to pose a threat across the southeastern United States today, including Georgia, the southern Appalachians, and extending west through much of central and northern Alabama, Mississippi, and Tennessee. Scattered power outages and downed trees and powerlines may occur, with the risk highest in elevated terrain.

Swells from Isaias will continue to affect much of the Gulf coasts of the United States, Mexico, and western Cuba this weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
A couple of tornadoes are possible today across eastern Georgia and the Carolinas.
